label: Opened our design system to coding agents: a generated manifest of every component, served to agents over MCP, so they read the system and use it the way our developers do, with a one-click setup for designers
Built the system I run three teams with: it reads the work where it happens, says how fresh and how sure every answer is, and drafts while I decide
Put agents on a schedule, with guardrails: a page of what's rolling out every weekday, and a draft of my Monday leadership update, both read-only and dry-run unless I say otherwise
Built a tool with agents for my talks in which structure and presentation are layers of one piece of work, viewed from either angle: the outline, or the live deck that exports to Keynote

Made the first commit of a telemetry plugin for my racing rig. By May it was a motorsport information system: a live HUD, race recording, and a dashboard that says whether tonight is a good night to race
Built native apps for iOS, macOS, Windows and Apple TV in four days, every one reading the same calculations from one API
Split one repository into seven, with a shared agents folder in each carrying every repository's instructions, so an agent working in one knows the rest
Drafted the Human Context Protocol with Claude: an open standard for how AI tools should talk to people, the other direction from MCP
Built a pipeline that turns OpenStreetMap roads and USGS elevation into tracks I can drive, and rebuilt its hard part three times. A track only counts once I've driven it

Took the cloud out of the racing system on purpose: once the racing service shipped its own tools and changed how outside apps sign in, a hosted version was the wrong bet. Racing Desk runs for one driver on one rig
Rebuilt KPT ShatterBox, the 1995 Illustrator filter I used as a designer, for Illustrator 2026, with an MCP server so agents can shatter artwork. It's the seed of the field behind this site
Started this site with agents
Researched the Cisco Meraki dashboard's fonts and the first design tokens for it
